summary.name: Shape Morphing (Motion Design and Cinematography). The source names this style explicitly.
summary.visualIdentity: Continuous contour morph between starting, intermediate and target forms, with trackable contour or semantic correspondence. It keeps center of gravity, direction and visual continuity, with holds at readable states. Crossfading alone does not qualify. Path order and holes must be controlled, and lettering must be verified after morphing.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: logo and icon transitions, and morphs that carry data meaning or recognizable silhouettes. Listed hybrids suggest data stories where chart forms change with item identity kept, and brand narratives using silhouette targets. Shared-element transitions are one application only, not the definition of the style.
summary.limitations: Morphing requires compatible contour structure. Mismatched segments, self-intersections or lost holes must be inspected, because intermediate shapes can collapse. Glyph morphs need validated outlines. mo.js covers only shape-property transitions, not arbitrary path morphing. The source note states that user-requested guidance does not verify every suggested detail in the source video. The keyword-glyph variant has only partial catalog support and cannot be reproduced exactly.
summary.palette: The background is scene-dependent: derive it from the subject, lighting and mood. #F5EFE2 is only an illustrative swatch, not a required canvas color. The example tokens #2F4348, #5C9790 and #CB8661 are unapproved suggestions, and any task-approved colors override them. Foreground on background measures 9.085:1, which passes normal text. Accent pairs are decorative-only. Gradients are disabled. Source reviews show flat saturated fields and flipping ink polarity, but they cover only sampled seconds 1 to 8.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Continuous, eased morphing with readable holds. Sharp cuts or stepped exposure are allowed where the action calls for them. The motion engine owns geometry, with one owner per animated property. Video state derives only from composition time, with no live pointer or scroll. Optional references motion-012, motion-014, motion-015, motion-038 and motion-039 apply only when scene assets support their defining action. Radial-burst confetti stays compact near the icon and never launches upward.
summary.audio: Unspecified. No audio is mandated or supplied. Options from audio_direction include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience or silence, chosen per topic. No verified music synchronization exists, and beat timing requires measured audio. Honor explicit user choices. Silence is valid.
summary.assetRequirements: No upload is mandatory. Optional inputs are starting, intermediate and target forms with compatible contours, and approved marks or glyphs with validated outlines. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering. Supplied exact colors and copy override the examples. Motion references need the actual scene illustration to validate their action. Do not invent brand marks or product copy.
summary.combinations: Suggested: style-097 for data encodings, where bars morph into pie segments with matched order and labels appear only at holds. Also suggested: style-043 for silhouettes with matched point counts and preserved center of gravity. Avoid mid-morph value distortion, crossfades and inconsistent holes.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: native SVG for geometry, masks and clips, with Paper.js only for compatible prepared path interpolation. Motion engine: GSAP MorphSVGPlugin for contour morphing, with Anime.js svg.morphTo as an optional alternative and Motion for optional DOM or SVG keyframes. HyperFrames owns composition timing, sync and export. Remotion is used only under its documented fallback condition, with the reason recorded. chroma-js validates colors. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks, plus decoded frame legibility.
